already_applied.line: - [x] Define the transformations under which a scientific GMI prediction should remain invariant: renaming, semantics-preserving recoding, compiler/substrate changes, equivalent grammar transformations, unit changes and equivalent state encodings. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z3-invariance-v1 IV-1: TRANSFORMATION_REGISTRY_V1.json registers 10 transformations covering all 6 named categories, 6 claimed-irrelevant and 4 declared-relevant, each carrying the exact quantity it must or must not move, with a machine check that every declared-relevant entry actually moves it.

- [x] Prove invariance/equivariance results under appropriate transformed resource accounting. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z3-invariance-v1 IV-2, IV-3: over 65552 candidates and 60 registered worlds the group generated by surface renaming, state-label negation and input/output conjugation preserves (bits, e_now, e_delay) candidate-wise with 0 alarms over 200 renamings, 0 sigma breaks on the whole universe and 0 mismatches against a direct full scan, while (eta,lambda) -> (c*eta,c*lambda) scales the objective and lambda* by exactly c with 0 equivariance breaks, so the verdict is a function of (p, lambda/eta) alone with boundary mu* = p/2.

- [x] Construct adversarial semantics-preserving recodings designed to flip morphology conclusions. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z3-invariance-v1 IV-4: 12544 of the 65536 declared-stateful candidates are behaviourally identical to a stateless one -- 8448 of them outside the 4096-member syntactic dead-table family -- and dead padding under mixed accounting/labelling conventions flips the morphology verdict on exactly 20 of the 60 registered worlds.

- [x] Require flagship conclusions to survive those recodings or explicitly characterize the non-invariant quantity. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z3-invariance-v1 IV-2, IV-4, IV-5: both branches delivered rather than the cheaper disjunct: the conclusions survive the claimed-irrelevant group on all 60 worlds, and the non-invariant quantity is identified as the declared state-bit count with exact census 12544 and invariant replacement bits_eff, which reproduces the declared verdict 60/60 and takes 0 flips under dead padding where the declared convention takes 40.

- [x] Quantify grammar-induced description-length and reachability bias. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z3-invariance-v1 IV-6: 21904 behavioural classes with multiplicity ratio exactly 785 and largest-class share 785/65552 against a uniform 1/21904; 16 classes at description length 4 bits against 21888 at 16; and under the frozen mutation graph 40198 of 65552 nodes lie within radius 8 of the registered start, the declared-stateless share of the ball falling from 1 at radius 0 to 15/214 at radius 3 against a universe share of 1/4097.

- [x] Identify control parameters producing morphology phase transitions. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z5-critical-phenomena-v1 CP-1: the objective is homogeneous of degree 1 in (eta, lambda), so the controls are exactly p and mu = lambda/eta -- 0 homogeneity violations over 60 worlds x a 6-rung rational scale ladder and 0 determinism violations across the 15 distinct (p, mu) keys -- with the argmin state-bit count as an order parameter jumping in {0,1}.

- [x] Derive critical thresholds analytically where possible. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z5-critical-phenomena-v1 CP-2: every one of the 16 stateless candidates has e_delay exactly N/2, so the best stateless cost is eta*p/2 and the best one-state-bit cost is lambda, giving lambda* = eta*p/2 by counting rather than enumeration; the analytic threshold equals the exact class-minimum crossing at all 60 worlds with 0 mismatches on both routes.

- [x] Predict behavior near transitions before measurement. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z5-critical-phenomena-v1 CP-3: registered in the freeze before the scan and confirmed: J* = min(eta*p/2, lambda) with 0 closed-form mismatches, an exact rational tie at lambda* on 20/20 boundary worlds, zero critical width at three probe offsets down to 1e-9, and a jump in dJ*/dlambda of exactly 1 -- equal to the order-parameter jump.

- [x] Test finite-size scaling. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z5-critical-phenomena-v1 CP-4: exhaustive re-enumeration of all 65552 candidates at L in {2,3,4,5} (N = 4, 16, 48, 128; 28, 146, 440, 444 distinct sigma classes) gives 0 threshold-drift violations at every rung, so the finite-size drift of lambda* is identically zero and the transition stays sharp at every size.

- [x] Test whether transition laws extrapolate across problem size and substrate. — ✅ gmi-833-z-z5-critical-phenomena-v1 CP-5: the law extrapolates exactly across problem size (zero drift in L) but NOT across substrate as scoped here: exhaustive enumeration of 16, 729 and 65536 A-ary stateless tables gives minimum delay fractions 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, so lambda*(A) = eta*p*(1 - 1/A) and the registered eta*p/2 is the A = 2 case only.
